items.summary: Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia drew varied responses across Asia as governments confirmed chip commitments, monitored projects, or addressed investigations. China dismissed spy allegations against a businesswoman linked to Alice Huang and denied reports tying restricted chips to a Shanghai data center. Singapore seized Alice Huang's passport over false server declarations before returning it for lack of evidence. South Korea received Nvidia's pledge of 260,000 advanced GPUs; Taiwan downplayed disruption while confirming its overseas headquarters plans remain on track; Japan vowed close monitoring.
items.title: Asian Governments React to Jensen Huang's Nvidia Exit

items.summary: Cursor disclosed a security breach that allowed attackers to distribute malicious versions of Anthropic's Claude Code extension through its VS Code marketplace on October 29. The attack originated from stolen credentials exposed via Fireworks AI, an infrastructure provider Cursor used for data sharing. Up to 5,000 developers may have received malware installing persistent SSH backdoors, though coding errors likely limited effectiveness. Malicious extensions versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 remained available for about 11 hours before removal. The breach exposed unredacted API credentials from AI coding-agent traces, enabling theft of non-production source code, customer data, and support information. This incident occurred amid a broader wave of attacks on AI developer platforms dubbed 'Black October' by Wiz.
items.title: Cursor Security Breach and Malicious Claude Code Extension Distribution

items.summary: Senator Andrew McLachlan warned that artists' copyright must not be sacrificed on the altar of corporate profit, demanding art over big tech. He raised constitutional concerns about watering down copyright as an illegal property acquisition. While Labor's Anthony Albanese called unpaid creatives 'theft,' AI firms like Anthropic seek legal certainty before investing. Coalition members Ross Cadell and Michaelia Cash backed Aria's concerns on just compensation.
items.title: Liberal Senator McLachlan Warns Against Sacrificing Artists' Copyright for AI Profit and Datacentre Expansion

items.summary: This article catalogs notable failures across the AI industry, framing them as lessons rather than a scorecard of flops. It notes that about 42% of corporate AI initiatives are abandoned (S&P Global Market Intelligence), citing reasons like weak funding and user demand. OpenAI rolled back its ChatGPT super-app redesign but successfully absorbed standalone apps; Sora shut down in March 2026 after high costs. Apple's delayed Siri finally launched via iOS 27 beta, contributing to a $250 million iPhone 16 settlement. Character.ai filed for bankruptcy in October 2026 amid legal and operational pressures despite earlier funding rounds totaling $150 million at a $1 billion valuation plus Google's $2.7 billion technology license deal.
items.title: The AI Graveyard: Startups and Products That Failed or Folded in 2024-2026

items.summary: Cmpnd released dspy-wsp, a prototype optimizer wrapping weight-space programming (WSP), where a frontier LLM reads and edits another model's weights directly—no gradients, training loop or fine-tuning data. Packaged as WeightSpace, it plugs into any DSPy program; tests used GPT-6-Astra on decision models from 0.6B to 9B parameters. On the Typed Decisions benchmark, d1-omni-600M rose from 50.9% to 69.1% (+18.3) with WeightSpace plus ReAnchor; alone it added 1.9–16.1 points. Gains fell at 9B (Clef-Flash +1.9), but the combination helped most there (+6.5). Runs were slow (78–167 minutes each, ~$5–10 in writer calls) and explicitly experimental.
items.title: Cmpnd Releases dspy-wsp: Weight-Space Programming Comes to DSPy

items.summary: On This Week in AI, the hosts examined frontier models moving into everyday services and the growing push for regional, responsible AI. OpenAI's LifeVal benchmark rose to roughly 80% on GPT-5.6 and GPT-6 Astra versus 49% for GPT-5.2; ChatGPT now handles about 20% of Google search-like queries. Anthropic tested read-only banking connections, released FlashProve, and METR reported AI may have doubled progress pace on some tasks. New research found Pashto questions used up to 179 times more energy than English ones. Countries are building local models—India's EKA-1 supports 22 languages; Indonesia, the UAE, and Uganda launched regional projects.
items.title: This Week in AI: Who Benefits from Progress?

items.summary: Stellantis filed US Patent No. 12,779,916 in 2023 for an electric tow dolly granted on November 3 (03NOV). The machine uses an onboard motor and battery to pull trailers while its regenerative braking and AI-backed steering keep control, letting small vehicles like the Fiat 500e act as lead cars instead of requiring a big truck. A patent signals no sale plans; it may simply block rivals from copying the concept.
items.title: Stellantis Patents AI-Powered Electric Tow Dolly That Turns Any Car Into a Towing Rig

items.summary: The Monetary Authority of Singapore opened its national currency vault, with room for 500 tons of bullion worth roughly $65BN at about $4,050 an ounce, to foreign central banks and sovereign entities. The launch follows a documented migration of privately held gold—over 800 tons in the city-state—to Singapore from New York and London. Private vaults can hold at least 2,200 tons between them, yet client holdings remain small relative to capacity. Demand is led by Western clients citing US fiscal deficits and political uncertainty; some European holders are reconsidering Swiss neutrality after frozen Russian assets. The sovereign facility offers a trusted Asian custodian alternative alongside the Bank of England and New York Fed. Storage alone does not create a market: liquidity, custody accounts for bullion banks, and an SGX clearing system matter more than the vault door. Gold trades well below January's record near $5,600 amid speculation dumping and Goldman targets of $4,150 year-end and $4,800 by end-2027.
items.title: Singapore Opens a $65 Billion Sovereign Gold Vault as Custody Shifts East

items.summary: Three years after the deadliest U.S. wildfires in over a century killed at least 102 people, displaced nearly 13,000 residents and destroyed more than 2,200 buildings — with only 15 percent rebuilt three years later — University of Hawaiʻi economists Ruben Juarez and biomedical scientist Alika Maunakea ran the Maui Wildfire Exposure Study (MauiWES) out of the Lahaina Comprehensive Health Center. The study has enrolled 2,500 participants over three years, combining testing with therapy, food assistance, cash support and insurance help; some survivors credit it with saving their lives. Researchers found widespread trauma in adults and children, plus elevated heavy metals linked to poor lung function. But federal renewal funding had stalled for more than a year after the Trump administration cut minority health programs, state legislation allotting $3 million failed at the last minute, and the Department of Health publicly disputed MauiWES's findings while withdrawing support.
items.title: Scientists Fight to Keep Maui Wildfire Health Study Alive Amid Funding Collapse

items.summary: The U.S. offshore wind industry has expanded even as President Trump's second-term policies threaten it. BloombergNEF cut its 2035 forecast from 39 gigawatts to 5.9 GW, yet this still represents extraordinary growth from the 30 MW deployed in 2016. Ørsted's $6.2-billion Revolution Wind came online with 704 MW capacity, becoming the third utility-scale farm fully operational after South Fork Wind and Vineyard Wind.
items.title: U.S. Offshore Wind Grows Despite Trump Crackdown

items.summary: Researchers at India's Vellore Institute of Technology tested a glazing system pairing transparent solar photovoltaic (TSPV) panels with transparent wood or bamboo. They evaluated 21 configurations, including an 8 mm-thick clear-glass reference and small cardboard building models measuring 12.5 cm on each side with a 5.5 cm × 5.5 cm skylight opening.
items.title: Transparent Bamboo Boosts Energy Performance of Solar PV Skylights

items.summary: On Nov. 7, Yanhe Technology launched three independently developed space photovoltaic modules aboard Galactic Energy's Ceres-2 Y3 rocket from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center at a 535 km sun-synchronous orbit. The mission validated China's first simultaneous in-orbit testing of perovskite-crystalline silicon and perovskite-CIGS tandem devices, plus a flexible single-junction module. Yanhe has not disclosed efficiencies or power outputs.
items.title: Yanhe Technology Launches Three Perovskite Solar Modules into Orbit

items.summary: A major Microsoft outage disrupted Outlook, Teams and Copilot across more than 70 countries since Thursday, affecting governments, hospitals, courts and businesses. Impacts reached Japan, the Philippines Supreme Court, Australia's intelligence agency, UK health services, Canada's railways, the US House of Representatives and India. Microsoft attributed the failure to a network capacity upgrade on Saturday morning and denied any cyberattack or AI-agent involvement, restoring all affected services while apologizing and promising a detailed report.
items.title: Microsoft Outage Disrupts Services in Over 70 Countries; Blamed on Network Upgrade, Not Cyberattack

items.summary: Rene Haas, chief executive of British semiconductor company Arm Holdings, has emerged as a potential successor to Jensen Huang at Nvidia after reports that the board approached him during its leadership search. According to Reuters, no final decision has been announced, and Haas is among several names being considered. Nvidia stated it is selecting a search firm, calling speculation about individual candidates premature. Colette Kress, the company's chief financial officer, currently serves as interim CEO.
items.title: Arm CEO Emerges as Potential Nvidia Successor

items.summary: Analysts expect the Bank of England, led by chief economist Huw Pill, to raise interest rates again soon amid forecasts that inflation will reach 5% next spring. Policymakers anticipate a rate rise from 4% to 4.25%, which would increase mortgage and business loan costs and pressure businesses to hike prices. The article challenges this view, arguing consumers have limited spare cash after years of austerity and shrinkflation. Instead, it points to the public sector—accounting for 25% of consumption—as a key driver of price increases through inflated infrastructure projects like HS2 (£11bn) and Thames crossing costs, plus rising consultant spending from £2.9bn in 2022-23 to £3.7bn in 2024-25.
items.title: UK Rate-Hike Debate and the Public Sector as an Inflationary Force

items.summary: New York has seen a dramatic uptick in lithium-ion battery fires from e-bikes and scooters, with 292 fires, 51 injuries and one death in 2025, versus more than 400 fires, 83 injuries and 12 deaths already this year. Deadly incidents include four family members killed in the Bronx and six people plus three firefighters and two police officers injured in Brooklyn. While e-bike popularity has grown—2.2 million imported into the U.S. in 2025—the city failed to build planned outdoor charging stations, with none completed despite a federal grant announced in 2023. Council Speaker Julie Menin called for safe storage mandates and an emergency oversight meeting on 20 November.
items.title: Rising ebike battery fires spark fear and stalled infrastructure response in New York City

items.summary: Narendra Modi's office summoned telecommunications secretary Amit Agrawal on Saturday to explain how officials ordered the takedown of more than 100 websites using fake court orders. Following a Reuters report that telecom officials directed providers to block 129 illegal betting sites based on forged High Court orders emailed by people posing as lawyers, state police launched a criminal investigation into potential forgery and cheating while an internal probe continues.
items.title: Modi's Office Summons Telecom Secretary Over Fake Court Orders

items.summary: Figure 1 plots the 10-year minus 3-month government term spread for Canada, France, Germany, Italy and the UK. The UK rose through September. Historically this spread predicted recessions better for Canada and Germany than elsewhere; assuming constant or near-zero default risk is typical of business-cycle analysis but seems implausible for France and Italy, as shown by their 5-year CDS.
items.title: 10-Year–3-Month Government Term Spreads in October

items.summary: The ABC News report frames Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang's resignation amid allegations of a relationship with tech executive Alice Huang as a cautionary tale about China's Ministry of State Security (MSS) using "honey trap" tactics. Former CIA officer Dennis Wilder describes how the MSS routinely targets American men in China, offering seduction followed by demands to cooperate and share sensitive information. The saga has prompted investigations from the FBI, Congress and Nvidia's board into whether Alice Huang was a Chinese asset who could have circumvented export controls on high-powered chips smuggled through her company Megaspeed. Former intelligence officials warn that while the US treats economic espionage as its top counterintelligence priority, it lacks an effective strategy to respond, leaving America at a disadvantage against China.
items.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang resignation exposes US vulnerability to Chinese espionage

items.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announced Saturday that Canada has concluded negotiations with the Philippines on a free trade deal, part of Ottawa's effort to reduce reliance on the United States amid tensions with Washington. The agreement is expected to be signed within about six months and come into force in 2027. Carney said it benefits sectors including agriculture, aerospace, AI, forest products, mining, energy and services.
items.title: Canada and Philippines Conclude Free Trade Talks

items.summary: This episode of a 12-episode series on China's Communist Party examines how it sustains unity while preserving collective decision-making. It warns that silence in meetings may mask unvoiced objections, letting problems go unreported and decisions become one person's judgment. The party addresses this through democratic centralism—reaffirmed at the Fifth Plenary Session of the 20th Central Committee—which pairs open discussion with disciplined action.
items.title: Setting the Rules Straight: Unity Through Collective Decision-Making

items.summary: Transport Secretary Sean Duffy said a nationwide ground stop causing thousands of cancellations stemmed from maintenance switching copper to fibre by contractor L3Harris, not a cyber-attack. A router flooding air traffic control systems prompted the closure. On Saturday over 3,500 flights were cancelled and more than 2,000 delayed. Duffy warned similar issues could recur without Congress approving upgrades; President Trump requested $30.1bn.
items.title: Copper-to-fibre wire upgrade triggered longest US airspace shutdown since 9/11

items.summary: Carmelle Collado won the first-ever Eurovision Song Contest held outside Europe, taking the Philippines' entry Sobra-Sobra to victory in Bangkok. She scored 211 points, finishing 41 clear of hosts Thailand with Vietnam third. The winner received most votes from both national juries and public ballot; half was decided before the show when juries voted at Friday's rehearsal, putting the Philippines top with 93 points ahead of Vietnam and Malaysia. Carmelle, 19, grew up in Bicol on Luzon and has competed since age 12. She said her Tagalog-English song celebrated female empowerment as a tribute to Filipino women. The show featured eleven countries competing over two and a half hours.
items.title: Philippines Wins First Eurovision Contest in Asia

items.summary: Victorian Aboriginal children advocate Meena Singh was alarmed by Premier Ben Carroll's $204m plan to detain youth offenders in secure facilities like Malmsbury. The proposal drew broad criticism from legal and union groups, who called it sentencing dressed up as leadership while crime rates rose under Labor. Polls show the party at historic lows—18% primary vote—and trailing the Coalition by 18 points on crime. MPs across factional lines worry the campaign's narrow focus abandons progressive achievements and cedes ground to the Greens, whose record high of 17% grew amid ticket disputes.
items.title: Victorian Labor MPs Divided Over Premier's 'Tough Love' Youth Detention Plan Amid Poll Slump

items.summary: The Philippines won the inaugural Eurovision Song Contest Asia, held at One Bangkok Arena with 11 countries competing. Nineteen-year-old Carmelle took first place with Sobra-Sobra, scoring 211 points (93 from juries, 118 public), ahead of Thailand's MANG x DAOU on 170 and Vietnam on 164.
items.title: Philippines Wins First-Ever Eurovision Song Contest Asia in Bangkok

items.summary: This episode of CPC's 12-episode series examines how China dismantles corruption networks shielding criminal activity, particularly in Southeast Asian scam centers aided by officials dubbed "protective umbrellas." The 20th Central Committee's Fifth Plenary Session calls for measures ensuring officials do not dare, cannot, or want to corrupt. In 2025, prosecutors charged 9,870 people with organized-crime offenses and 65 as protective umbrellas—underscoring that lasting reform requires dismantling networks, not just punishing individuals.
items.title: Setting the Rules Straight: When Crime Wears a Suit

items.summary: Will Joseph scored a record-equalling five tries, including one from his first touch inside 65 seconds and three more before the interval, as England beat Japan 78-15 at Twickenham on Nov 14. George Ford converted three tries; Freddie Steward, Ellis Genge, Cadan Murley, Ben Earl scored in an eight-try first half, with Martin, Curry, Smith and Fisilau after the break. Harry Hockings' yellow card became a 20-minute red.
items.title: England's Record-Breaking Rout of Japan in Nations Championship Opener

items.summary: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy escalated criticism of SpaceX on Nov 14, saying speed restrictions on its military-grade Starshield terminals had dangerous political implications and undermined air defenses. He said terminals in temporarily Russian-occupied territories were limited to 161 kph for five days, hampering Ukraine's capabilities. The Defence Ministry raised the issue institutionally. Zelenskyy denied a technical explanation, calling it partial recognition of occupied territory. SpaceX denies introducing new restrictions.
items.title: Zelenskyy Escalates Criticism of SpaceX Over Starshield Speed Caps

items.summary: Public health experts in Perth are set to endorse the 'Perth Declaration,' a global plan to eliminate acute rheumatic fever (ARF) and rheumatic heart disease (RHD) by 2040, arguing that prevention methods already exist but political will is lacking. Australia's national Endgame Strategy aims to end RHD by 2031, yet World Health Federation head Jagat Narula noted only a small proportion of the $689 million required has been committed, with the federal government citing $95.8 million in funding announced in 2021 over six years. The disease disproportionately affects First Nations Australians and Pacific peoples, who face high rates linked to overcrowded housing and poor hygiene rather than lack of resources.
items.title: Australia's Rheumatic Heart Disease Eradication Plan Faces Funding and Political Shortfalls

items.summary: At COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, UN climate chief Simon Stiell urged negotiators to avoid tactical delays as delegates from over 200 nations seek a deal capping warming at 2 degrees Celsius. Tens of thousands protested amid frustration that inflation, wars and debt overshadow the agenda, with the US absent under President Trump.
items.title: COP31 in Antalya Faces Delay Tactics Amid Global Protests and Climate Urgency

items.summary: In Shenzhen, a Chinese technology hub hosting APEC this week, aerial food deliveries are common over busy tourist areas. The piece frames the city as emblematic of how drones ease life for delivery drivers and hungry visitors on the move. It asserts that China has become one of the world's most advanced markets for commercial drone logistics.
items.title: Shenzhen Leads China's Commercial Drone Delivery Boom

items.summary: Thousands took to the streets across France on Saturday for its fifth consecutive day of nationwide protests, with turnout lower than usual. Organisers estimated around 200,000 demonstrators nationally and 100,000 in Paris, versus an interior ministry estimate of about 106,000 people (including 24,000 in the capital). Protests reflected frustration over rising living costs, education funding, a new police bill dubbed 'license to kill', and alleged police brutality. The unions have called for another strike next Tuesday after rejecting a proposed minimum wage increase of 0.6%.
items.title: France's Fifth Consecutive Saturday of Nationwide Protests

items.summary: TRNC Prime Minister Unal Ustel condemned the burning of Turkish and TRNC flags by Greek Cypriot youths during protests marking the TRNC's 43rd anniversary on November 14, 2026. He described the acts as an attack on the honor of the Turkish nation and blamed the Greek Cypriot Administration for fostering hostility in schools. Ustel called for immediate action against those responsible.
items.title: Turkish Cypriot premier condemns burning of Turkish and TRNC flags in Southern Cyprus

items.summary: Greenpeace activists dumped about 15 metric tons of boulders on the seabed off England's Norfolk coast to block bottom trawling. Most rocks fell within the designated area for the £12 billion ($15.86 billion) Norfolk Vanguard East wind farm, part of an RWE and UK government deal with construction expected next year. The group says energy companies routinely move natural boulders before building farms.
items.title: Greenpeace Seabed Protest Threatens North Sea Wind Farm

items.summary: China's growing influence in Southeast Asia is increasingly tied to military cooperation, not just trade or infrastructure. In late September 2025, China and Laos opened a joint military support and training center near Vientiane, where Laotian pilots will initially be trained at the Ban Keun airfield. Earlier in 2025, China expanded its footprint at Cambodia's Ream naval base on the Gulf of Thailand for logistics and training. Experts like Marco Bünte note these facilities could give China strategic depth in mainland Southeast Asia and better access to the South China Sea, though he cautions against speaking of military hegemony. Johann Fuhrmann emphasizes distinguishing between Laotian pilot training and any future use by Chinese forces. The Ban Keun runway's 2,000-meter length limits it for large bombers requiring 3,000 meters. Smaller nations are hedging their relationships while Vietnam and the Philippines watch closely amid South China Sea disputes.
items.title: New facilities in Laos and Cambodia: Is China expanding its military presence in Southeast Asia?

items.summary: On Friday, Burkina Faso issued arrest warrants and extradition requests for around 20 people including exiled journalists, activists, an ex-minister, and former military officers. They are accused of terrorism-related charges such as complicity in terrorist activities, financing terrorism, and glorification of terrorism; alleged defamation, undermining morale of the National Armed Forces, and contempt of public authority are also mentioned.
items.title: Burkina Faso Issues Arrest Warrants for Around 20 People Including Journalists

items.summary: The FAA lifted a rare nationwide ground stop on Friday, the longest since September 2001 and first since January 2023. Outdated air traffic communications equipment overloaded with data triggered it, affecting regional control centers that Duffy blamed on lack of Congressional funding. With roughly 10,000 flights cancelled, he warned departures would resume gradually over days. He called for $50 billion in system upgrades.
items.title: US Nationwide Ground Stop Lifted After Longest Shutdown Since 2001

items.summary: Social animals must agree on where and when to move, rest or settle. Chimpanzees use a vocal “rest hoo” that prolongs breaks longer the more often it is called; golden snub-nosed monkeys require at least four votes for a destination proposal and three supporters before departure becomes likely; vulturine guineafowl let subordinates initiate movement when dominants monopolize food, in what researchers call the “losers who lead” mechanism; and gorillas rely on collective vocal choruses to time departures. American cockroaches show that decisions depend on social feedback rather than a majority: robots laced with pheromones persuaded real insects toward an unusual shelter despite being outnumbered.
items.title: How Animals Reach Collective Decisions—and How Their Choices Can Be Manipulated

items.summary: Maryanne Wolf argues that reading is not innate but a learned circuit linking vision, language, cognition, motor skills and affect. She warns of 'use it or lose it,' comparing today's shift to digital media with ancient Greece's slow 400-year acceptance of writing. Unlike the Greeks, she says we have only years to understand what screens displace—skimming short-circuits deep reading by bypassing attention and effort. While acknowledging new visual-motor functions emerge, Wolf stresses preserving evaluative judgment against external knowledge platforms like AI, which can mislead when over-relied upon.
items.title: Neuroscientist Maryanne Wolf on Reading, Screens and Cognitive Decline

items.summary: Japan is considering capping its five-year defense spending at around ¥60 trillion while revising three key national security documents by year's end. The Defense Ministry estimates needs of ¥70–80 trillion, whereas the Finance Ministry argues for below ¥60 trillion. With Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi reportedly reluctant to raise taxes, a funding battle between ministries is intensifying.
items.title: Japan Weighs ¥60 Trillion Five-Year Defense Spending Plan Amid Ministry Dispute

items.summary: In a Friday speech, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio issued an aggressive challenge to international law, warning that the United States would never submit to what he called radical judges or soulless global bureaucrats. He dismissed such law as an instrument elites use for their own interests, telling critics to stop quoting laws against those with power.
items.title: Rubio Labels International Law a Tool of Elites and Attacks ICC

items.summary: An analysis by anti-corruption group DeKleptocracy found that President Trump bought between $1 million and $5 million worth of Nvidia stock before his administration scrapped a Biden-era export rule in May 2025, easing restrictions on advanced AI chip sales to China. His disclosures also showed purchases across Apple, Meta, and Microsoft. The reversal enabled Nvidia's H200 chips—six times more powerful than those available in China—to sell after Commerce approval in January 2026, drawing national security concerns. Trump made at least three additional Nvidia purchases of $250,001 to $500,000 each following the announcement, amid scrutiny over alleged ties between Alice Huang and Jensen Huang.
items.title: Trump's Nvidia Stock Purchases and China Chip Export Reversal

items.summary: RBI granted Mufin Green Finance an Authorised Dealer Category-II licence, enabling fee-based forex conversion, Liberalised Remittance Scheme remittances (education, medical treatment, travel), family maintenance transfers, and smaller trade-related services. The capital-light vertical aims to diversify revenue beyond net interest income. For Q2 FY27 ended September 2026, the NBFC's net profit more than doubled to ₹15 crore from ₹6 crore a year earlier; total income rose to ₹90 crore from ₹49 crore; gross NPA improved to 1.77% from 2.37%; and capital adequacy ratio stood at 27.73%. MD Kapil Garg expects revenue doubling over the coming year.
items.title: Mufin Green Finance Earns RBI AD-II Licence for Forex and Remittance Services

items.summary: As President Donald Trump prepares to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping in China next week, the affair between former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy is intensifying US-China tensions over artificial intelligence. Lawmakers on both sides are pressing for tighter export restrictions amid fears Beijing could exploit access to leaders like Huang. While Nvidia's sales to China have plummeted from roughly 95% market share due to earlier restrictions, its advanced chips remain crucial for many Chinese AI firms. Analysts warn the scandal may derail ongoing US-China AI safety talks and accelerate efforts toward technological self-reliance.
items.title: Nvidia scandal heightening America's AI rivalry with China ahead of Trump's visit

items.summary: Under a proposed US-India bilateral trade agreement, the United States has assured India of a comparative tariff advantage over rival exporters such as Vietnam, Bangladesh and China, though officials caution that the benefit depends on the final tariff structure and ongoing investigations. The first tranche is expected by year-end, with services deferred to later talks. Currently, Vietnam faces a 12.5% Section 301 duty while Bangladesh faces 10%, both above MFN rates; India itself received an additional 10% levy effective July 24, 2026 following forced-labour findings. Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal expressed confidence in securing one of the best deals. Analysts warn that a tariff edge alone may not help Indian exporters overtake rivals, as manufacturing costs, capacity and logistics remain decisive.
items.title: US Tariff Advantage for India vs. Vietnam and Bangladesh

items.summary: The Sharad Pawar-led Nationalist Congress Party (NCP-SP) dismissed reports of a merger with the Ajit Pawar faction as "completely false," saying it has no plans to join any party. Spokesperson Pravin Kunte Patil alleged the rumors were meant to distract from drought, inflation and other issues. Working president Supriya Sule said merger talks had ended after her late cousin Ajit Pawar died; she received no contact from the faction—"not a single phone call." She rejected NDA-joining speculation, declined to comment on senior leaders like Chhagan Bhujbal, and urged media focus on policy issues such as the FCRA Bill. Sule also dismissed personal meetings with Praful Patel as institutional committee work.
items.title: NCP (SP) Rejects Merger Buzz After Ajit Pawar's Death

items.summary: On Saturday, Karnataka chief minister D K Shivakumar recalled Prime Minister Narendra Modi paying for his ticket during their first ride together on Bengaluru's newly inaugurated metro Pink Line. Shivakumar said he did not have money at the time and that Modi swiped his own smart card to cover the fare.
items.title: Karnataka CM Recalls Modi Paying for His Metro Ticket on Bengaluru Pink Line

items.summary: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar said Saturday that the China border has become 'more alive,' demanding sustained troop commitment, citing infrastructure gains since the 2020 Galwan clash: new tunnels, bridges and airfields built with growing frequency over the past decade. On trade, he described India-US negotiations as near the finishing line, seeking a balanced deal giving India comparative advantage.
items.title: Jaishankar on India-China Border and US Trade Deal Progress

items.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said India and the United States have resolved most outstanding issues in their proposed trade agreement, including tariff matters, with negotiations entering a final phase. Speaking at the HT Leadership Summit in Delhi on November 14, he expressed optimism that both sides are approaching the finishing line, noting remaining concerns largely stem from developments on the American side. The development carries significance ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's likely December 14-15 visit to Miami for the G20 Summit, where he may meet US President Donald Trump and review bilateral relations.
items.title: India-US Trade Deal Nears Finalisation as Modi Prepares for G20 Visit

items.summary: At the 31st CII Partnership Summit in Visakhapatnam (Nov 2026), Andhra Pradesh's Economic Development Board signed nine MoUs. Eight propose investments totalling Rs 4,100 crore and 6,865 direct jobs across Sri Sathya Sai, Tirupati, Nellore and Visakhapatnam; the ninth is a five-year Pawan Hans heliport partnership.
items.title: Andhra Pradesh Signs Nine MoUs for Space Sector Push Worth Rs 4,100 Crore

items.summary: A 27-year-old Indian-origin man, Bilal Kazi, was sentenced to 30 years' imprisonment at Chester Crown Court on November 13 after pleading guilty to child sexual abuse offences. He posed online as a white British teenager named 'Reece', using Snapchat, Roblox and Wink to groom girls aged 11 to 17 across 28 of the UK's 45 police forces; investigators identified 70 victims from an initial pool of 180 potential ones. His methods escalated from sharing explicit images to blackmail after refusals, with some contacts lasting over a year. More than 400 indecent items were recovered in Cheshire and more than 500 on Birmingham devices.
items.title: Bilal Kazi Sentenced for Online Grooming of Dozens of Girls in UK

items.summary: BJP MLA Shagun Parihar alleged that the bodies of two Special Police Officers, Rashpal Singh and Bobby Chand, killed in Jammu and Kashmir's Kishtwar district on Wednesday after gunfire near Deharna forest, were transported to their native village Keyar without coffins. Found Thursday about two kilometres away with service weapons missing, they had been part of a team relieving an Army unit at Basnan.
items.title: BJP MLA Alleges Kishtwar Cops' Bodies Brought Without Coffins

items.summary: A Jharkhand man, Samir Pan of Narsanda village under Muffasil police station area, killed his two-and-a-half-year-old cousin on November 11 after viewing her as an obstacle to leaving with her mother for whom he had an extramarital relationship. Police recovered the body from a West Singhbhum nullah and arrested him; officer-in-charge Vinod Kumar said Pan confessed during questioning before being sent to judicial custody, per Press Trust of India.
items.title: Jharkhand Man Kills Toddler in Affair-Related Motive; Arrested and Sentenced to Judicial Custody

items.summary: A Canadian forestry company has donated more than 1,800 hectares of forest, wetlands and freshwater shoreline near Gander Lake to support a major conservation initiative. The donation from Domtar will allow the Nature Conservancy of Canada (NCC) to protect four parcels along the Southwest Gander River and Gander Lake, close to Glenwood and Appleton. Announced on October 1, 2025, it is described as NCC's largest land donation in Atlantic Canada during its 54 years of work there. The project aims to improve wildlife movement across connected habitats while safeguarding ecosystems where less than 3% of the Central Newfoundland ecoregion falls under conservation status.
items.title: Canadian firm donates 1,800 hectares to reconnect wildlife habitat

items.summary: Authoritarian regimes routinely conceal escalating disasters even when secrecy harms their own citizens and neighbours. With climate change predicted to increase weather-related catastrophes, governments' willingness to share information transnationally is a growing concern. Recent examples include China's tight control of reporting on Nepal-Tibet border floods in 2025, Russia hiding damage from Siberia's Ishim River overflow in 2025, Ethiopia under Mengistu downplaying the 1984 famine that killed an estimated one million people while spending over US$100 million on celebrations, and Myanmar blocking aid after a 7.7-magnitude earthquake in April 2025. Chernobyl's cover-up may have caused between 100,000 and 250,000 additional deaths across Belarus, Ukraine and Russia. Such censorship risks over-extracting shared water sources, delaying disease responses, accelerating refugee crises, and compromising citizens' safety as climate-driven incidents escalate.
items.title: When Authoritarian Regimes Censor Disaster News, Everyone Suffers

items.summary: Nationalist Congress Party leader Supriya Sule told reporters that the government had not submitted any fresh delimitation proposal or Bill, though her party would consider a uniform 50 per cent seat increase positively. She cited rising electorate sizes—12-13 lakh voters when she first contested versus 25-40 lakh today—as justification for redistricting.
items.title: NCP's Supriya Sule on Delimitation and No Fresh Proposal

items.summary: A Telangana cadre IAS officer, Rajeevgandhi Hanumanthu (2012 batch), along with family members, was injured Saturday when their car collided with a school van near Chaparallapalli village in Ananthasagaram mandal of Nellore district while traveling on National Highway-565 from Tirumala to Srisailam. The injured were first taken to the government hospital at Atmakur for emergency care, then shifted by Endowments Minister Anam Ramanarayana Reddy to a private hospital in Nellore.
items.title: Telangana IAS Officer and Family Injured in Car-Van Collision on Highway-565

items.summary: A 20-year-old man, Yash Singh of Airoli in Navi Mumbai, was arrested on Saturday after allegedly conducting reconnaissance of sensitive South Mumbai locations—including the Chabad House and Jewish-owned businesses—on behalf of international criminal syndicates. Initially detained by Maharashtra ATS based on social media contacts with anti-national handlers, he later came into custody via Kerala police over a Thrissur case. Singh admitted photographing targets around Colaba for money received from Telegram-linked mafia gangs.
items.title: Man Held for Reconnaissance of Sensitive Mumbai Locations

items.summary: Police arrested two people, Suresh and Meenakshi, including a woman possibly an influencer, in the multi-crore Madurai Tanishq jewellery heist. CCTV footage from the showroom on Madurai Bypass Road proved crucial after an employee identified Nishanth, the prime suspect still at large. Investigators probe whether Meenakshi helped him dispose of or move the loot; Suresh's role remains unclear. The robbery occurred early November 12 via scaffolding and a lift maintenance area.
items.title: Two Arrested in Madurai Tanishq Heist; Hunt Continues for Prime Suspect

items.summary: Literary hotels captivate visitors by linking real buildings to the worlds of literature, falling into three overlapping categories: places tied to writers' lives and work, sites offering glimpses of creative circumstances, and locations absorbed directly into fiction. Burgh Island Hotel in South Devon exemplifies this last type; its cliffs, tidal causeway and isolation inspired Agatha Christie's novels, including Evil Under the Sun (1936), transforming geographical features into engines of suspense. Similarly, Jamaica Inn on Bodmin Moor drew on Daphne du Maurier's misty riding experience for her 1936 novel. Thomas Hardy's King's Arms Hotel in Dorchester illustrates how a single building can belong both to biography and fiction through his invented region of Wessex. Ultimately, these hotels make visible the ongoing relationship between literature and reality.
items.title: The Enduring Appeal of Literary Hotels

items.summary: The Panvel Municipal Corporation (PMC) has proposed dedicated 'Pink Toilets' to improve safe public sanitation for women amid rapid urbanisation. Planned through public-private partnerships and CSR funding under the Mahila Sanman Swachhata Abhiyan with Swachh Bharat Mission support, facilities would include Indian-style and automatic toilets, sanitary napkin vending machines, incinerators, breastfeeding rooms, solar power, CCTV, security staff and QR feedback codes. A pilot at three sites—Gango Garden near CKT High School, KLE College in Kalamboli and the Hiranandani bus stop in Kharghar—is planned, with 25 to 50 high-footfall locations identified for the first phase across Panvel, Kharghar, Mansarovar and Khanda Colony.
items.title: Panvel Municipal Corporation Proposes Pink Toilets At Busy Locations, 3 Sites Identified For Pilot Project

items.summary: Per NDTV, Pakistan's ISI moved Hafiz Saeed of Lashkar-e-Taiba from Lahore to Rawalpindi and JeM chief Masood Azhar to a safe house in Nawabshah over the past week. Both leaders reportedly limit contact with their groups amid fears of Indian strikes after Operation Sindoor damaged terror infrastructure, though Pakistan claims they remain imprisoned.
items.title: Pakistan Relocates Saeed and Azhar Amid Indian Strike Fears

items.summary: Darbhanga police traced three girls aged 10, 12, and 15 who went missing from the Biraul area on November 8, hours after constituting a special investigation team (SIT) led by city superintendent of police Ashok Kumar. The girls were found aboard a passenger bus traveling from Darbhanga to Biraul Saturday evening.
items.title: Darbhanga Police Recover Three Missing Girls Hours After Forming SIT

items.summary: A 20-year-old man, Yash Singh, was arrested in Navi Mumbai after allegedly conducting reconnaissance of sensitive locations including the Chabad/Nariman House targeted in the November 26-11 terror attack. Working under suspected foreign handlers, he collected photographs and details on Jewish nationals and their establishments. The case links to a UAPA matter in Thrissur, Kerala, implicating the Pakistan-based Shahzad Bhatti network in recruiting vulnerable youth via social media.
items.title: 20-year-old arrested for reconnaissance of Nariman House ahead of Mumbai terror attacks

items.summary: A SoftBank‑backed vehicle, SVF II Meerkat (DE) LLC, sold 7.64 crore Meesho shares at Rs 246.75 each on Friday in a block deal worth over Rs 1,885 crore on the NSE, reducing its stake from 6.84% to 5.19%. Buyers included Societe Generale as the largest purchaser (over 1.47 crore shares for Rs 364.65 crore), alongside domestic and foreign institutional investors. SoftBank had earlier sold stakes in Lenskart Solutions (Rs 1,896 crore) and Meesho (Rs 1,650 crore).
items.title: SoftBank's Continued Offloading of Indian E‑Commerce and Retail Equities via SVF II Meerkat

items.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi seeking inclusion of the state's 2023 reservation Act in the Constitution's Ninth Schedule. The law raised Scheduled Castes reservation from 15% to 17% and Scheduled Tribes from 3% to 7%, but a High Court judgment on October 12 struck it down, holding aggregate reservation at 56% exceeded the 50% ceiling.
items.title: DK Shivakumar writes to PM Modi, seeks ninth schedule protection for Karnataka's 56% quota
